text: Federated classifiers can appear reliable on average yet become unsafe when future traffic shifts toward a difficult client. This study asks which predictions from a fixed federated open-set classifier may be automated when the client mixture is only partially known. Client-dependent acceptance changes the mixture among automated predictions, so the relevant selective risk is a ratio whose numerator and denominator both depend on traffic. FedCORE represents traffic uncertainty by a credal set and sampling uncertainty by finite-sample client audits. Using only audit size, accepted count, and accepted-error count, it returns a deploy-or-refuse decision without retraining. We establish a fixed-pooling reducibility boundary, an exact full-simplex certificate, a positive-denominator program for strict credal polytopes, and familywise-valid selection among proposal-frozen rules. In target-matched replay over 443 proposal-feasible empirical-reservoir conditions, the minimum observed coverage was 0.953 and none fell below 0.95. In an Office-Home sensitivity analysis, an independently formed traffic confidence set changed the protected target and increased certifications from 74 to 92 of 100 and mean effective certified acceptance from 9.6% to 19.3%. A prospectively sealed post-incident fresh-seed PACS rerun completed all 30 models, but each procedure certified only three and mean effective certified acceptance remained below 4%. The PACS experiment therefore produced a complete negative result under the predeclared utility gates. Together, the results distinguish validity of a credal deployment decision from utility of the underlying predictor.
